text:
maria: FYI ran into a nasty runtime error after shading our client into the app jar. stack trace shows NoSuchMethodError on ObjectMapper.findAndRegisterModules().

maria: minimal stack:
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper.findAndRegisterModules()Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ObjectMapper;
  at com.redwood.client.JsonHelpers.configureMapper(JsonHelpers.kt:42)
  ...
```

maria: I'm using Gradle shadowJar relocate for com.fasterxml.jackson -> com.redwood.shaded.fasterxml. Any pointers? also streaming NDJSON endpoints sometimes fail with Gson when reading chunked responses.

alex: Can you paste the shadow config? often missing relocating jackson-module-kotlin or module metadata causes mismatch.

maria: here's the relevant bit from build.gradle.kts:
```kts
shadowJar {
  relocate("com.fasterxml.jackson", "com.redwood.shaded.fasterxml.jackson")
  relocate("okhttp3", "com.redwood.shaded.okhttp3")
  minimize()
}
```

sam: ah - minimize() can drop service descriptors. Also relocate needs to match all jackson packages (jackson-core, jackson-annotations, jackson-databind, jackson-module-kotlin). Try explicit relocates and keep the kotlin module.

alex: also watch for mixed versions: if the runtime (app server) already has a different jackson on the classpath, shading + relocating might still conflict if some libs expect the unshaded package (reflection/service loaders). Two options:
- relocate everything and bundle *all* jackson deps (and disable minimize), or
- don't shade jackson; shade only okhttp/third-party to avoid collisions.

jen: small related note — if you're adding Authorization in an application interceptor and hitting 301/302, OkHttp can drop auth on redirect. Use a network interceptor to inject auth so it survives redirects, or use OkHttpClient.Builder.followRedirects(false) and handle manually. We saw similar header-drop behavior in 4.9 -> 4.10 changes.

drew: for the NDJSON + Gson chunking issue: Gson.fromJson on an InputStreamReader can choke when chunks boundary split tokens. Use Gson's JsonReader in lenient mode, or better: switch to Jackson streaming (MappingIterator) which handles incremental parsing nicely. Example with Jackson: 
```java
MappingIterator<MyEvent> it = new ObjectMapper().readerFor(MyEvent.class).readValues(inputStream);
while (it.hasNext()) { process(it.next()); }
```
This works well with chunked NDJSON.

maria: good call. I switched to Jackson streaming readValues and that fixed the partial-chunk failures. For the NoSuchMethodError the fix was to remove minimize(), add explicit relocates for:
- com.fasterxml.jackson.core => com.redwood.shaded.jackson.core
- com.fasterxml.jackson.databind => com.redwood.shaded.jackson.databind
- com.fasterxml.jackson.module.kotlin => com.redwood.shaded.jackson.module.kotlin
and include the kotlin module JAR in the shadow.

alex: if you must shade, also relocate internal jackson package-level annotations and register modules via the shaded package path if your code references the original com.fasterxml names via reflection. Another trick: call ObjectMapper.registerModule(KotlinModule()) explicitly instead of relying on findAndRegisterModules(), avoids the reflective lookup that failed.

sam: for long-term maintainability I'd recommend: don't shade jackson; instead:
- shade okhttp and other vendored libs
- declare jackson as a provided/runtime dependency and ensure a single canonical version in the platform
This reduces weird runtime surprises.

jen: bumping OkHttp to latest 4.11 also helped our redirect/auth edgecases. Worth trying if you rely on network interceptor semantics.

maria: thanks everyone, repro plan: revert minimize(), add explicit relocates, switch NDJSON client to Jackson MappingIterator, and test against staging with the server that injects chunked events. I'll ping once I have a PR. :thumbsup:

alex: cheers — ping me for a quick review when the PR is up.

drew: I can add a small integration test that spins up a chunked NDJSON server and asserts incremental parsing works.

maria: appreciated!
